title: feat(rules): add a corpus manifest with an expected-findings schema
problem: Corpus expectations are implicit (a `positive.rs` must trigger, a `negative.rs` must not), which cannot express counts, severities, or multi-rule files.
why: An explicit schema makes regression intent reviewable and enables stronger assertions.
scope: Add an `expected.json` per corpus rule directory listing expected rule ids, counts, and severities.
Validate the manifest in the corpus test and fail on mismatch.
guidance: Keep the schema small and documented; support optional fields for forward compatibility.
acceptance: Every rule has a valid manifest

title: test(rules): add false-negative coverage for every detector
problem: The corpus verifies positives trigger, but there is no curated set of known-vulnerable samples that must never be missed.
why: Tracking recall prevents silent regressions where a refactor stops detecting a real pattern.
scope: Add a `must-trigger` fixture per detector based on the original vulnerability rationale.
guidance: Document why each sample is a true positive.
acceptance: Every detector has at least one must-trigger sample

title: feat(tooling): add a rule scaffold generator
problem: Adding a rule requires manually creating a module, metadata, fixtures, docs, and registration lines.
why: A generator lowers the barrier and enforces the checklist, improving rule consistency.
scope: Generate a rule module, corpus directories, a docs stub, and the registration line from an id and title.
guidance: Make it idempotent and refuse to overwrite existing files.
acceptance: Generated rule compiles and passes validation after editing placeholders
tests: Unit test of the generator in a temporary directory
security: Generator must not create files outside the repository.

title: feat(tooling): add a corpus coverage report
problem: There is no quick way to see which rules lack negatives, must-trigger samples, or documentation.
why: Visibility into corpus gaps drives contributions where they matter.
scope: Add a report listing per-rule fixture counts, docs presence, and validation status.
guidance: Support terminal and markdown output; keep it read-only.
acceptance: Report generated in CI or on demand
tests: Unit test on the current corpus

title: test(rules): snapshot expected finding counts to detect regressions
problem: A refactor that changes how many findings the corpus produces can go unnoticed if the corpus only checks non-empty results.
why: Exact-count snapshots catch accidental broadened or narrowed matching.
scope: Record per-rule finding counts for the corpus and compare on every test run.
guidance: Update the snapshot deliberately in the PR that changes behavior, with justification.
security: Changes to counts must be reviewed as detection changes.

title: feat(rules): add a rule deprecation process and mechanism
problem: There is no way to retire a rule without deleting its id and breaking baselines.
why: Rule ids must remain stable; deprecation preserves compatibility while reducing noise.
scope: Add a `deprecated` flag to rule metadata that keeps the id resolvable but excludes it from default execution.
Warn when a baseline or config references a deprecated rule.
guidance: Document the deprecation lifecycle and a minimum deprecation window.
acceptance: Deprecated rules are documented and skipped by default
security: Never silently drop a rule without a deprecation notice.

title: test(rules): add adversarial fixtures for each detector
problem: Detectors are not stressed with inputs designed to evade or overwhelm them.
why: Adversarial fixtures reveal both false negatives and pathological cost.
scope: Add per-rule fixtures using macros, aliases, whitespace tricks, and unusual but valid syntax.
guidance: Document expected behavior (trigger or not) for each adversarial sample.
acceptance: Each detector has at least one adversarial fixture
